name: Cyclops
summary: The X-Man who can never simply open his eyes. Scott Summers fires nonstop force beams held back only by ruby-quartz lenses, and he has spent decades leading Xavier's mutants.
origin: Cyclops can never just open his eyes without thinking about it, and that one detail explains his whole personality. Scott Summers was Professor Xavier's first recruit when The X-Men #1 launched in 1963, a mutant whose eyes constantly fire beams of concussive force that only ruby-quartz lenses can hold back. One slip of the visor and the room comes apart. Living under that kind of control turned him into a natural leader: a sharp strategist, a capable fighter and a skilled pilot who has steered the X-Men through more crises than anyone. Fans love to call him a boy scout, but he is the most quietly intense person on the team.
powers: Constant force beams from his eyes
Instinctive feel for angles and trick shots

storyline.title: Xavier's first student
storyline.beat: Scott Summers is the field leader of the original X-Men in their first issue. His eyes fire uncontrollable force beams, held back only by a ruby-quartz visor.

storyline.title: Losing Jean
storyline.beat: Scott watches Jean Grey give her life at the end of the Dark Phoenix Saga, and soon leaves the X-Men to grieve.

storyline.title: Marriage and a messy exit
storyline.beat: Scott marries Madelyne Pryor and they have a son, Nathan. When Jean is found alive he leaves to join X-Factor, a move many readers still hold against him.

storyline.title: Scott and Jean marry
storyline.beat: After decades of romance, Scott and Jean finally marry in X-Men #30 (1994).

storyline.title: Mutant general
storyline.beat: With mutants nearly extinct, Scott runs covert strike teams, moves the X-Men to the island of Utopia, and splits with Wolverine over how to protect young mutants.

storyline.title: Phoenix-possessed
storyline.beat: Empowered by the Phoenix Force, Scott loses control and kills Charles Xavier, becoming a fugitive and a radical symbol for mutantkind.

gossip.text: Cyclops shoots heat lasers from his eyes.
gossip.truth: In the comics his optic blasts are concussive force with no heat. They punch rather than burn.

gossip.text: He cannot switch his beams off. The usual explanation is a head injury from a childhood plane crash.
Cable is his son. Scott and Madelyne Pryor's baby Nathan was sent to the future and came back as a grizzled soldier.
Scott and his brother Havok are largely immune to each other's energy powers.
Leaving his wife and baby for a newly returned Jean in 1986 is still one of the most-debated character moves in X-Men history.

quiz.q: What material is Cyclops's visor lens made from?
quiz.why: Ruby quartz holds back his optic blasts.

quiz.q: Which mutant is Cyclops's younger brother?
quiz.why: Alex Summers, also known as Havok.

quiz.q: Who did Scott Summers marry in 1994?
quiz.why: Scott and Jean married in X-Men #30 (1994).

timeline.title: Xavier's first student
timeline.note: The X-Men #1 introduces Scott Summers as the stiff, serious field leader of a school for young mutants.

timeline.title: Losing Jean on the moon
timeline.note: The Dark Phoenix Saga ends with Jean sacrificing herself in front of Scott, the heartbreak that defines him.

timeline.title: Founding X-Factor
timeline.note: X-Factor #1 reunites the five original X-Men, a messy move since Scott leaves a wife and baby to chase Jean.

timeline.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
timeline.note: The Fox Kids cartoon makes Scott the visor-wearing leader for a whole generation of Saturday-morning fans.

timeline.title: Finally marrying Jean
timeline.note: X-Men #30 gives Scott and Jean the big wedding fans spent decades waiting for.

timeline.title: James Marsden in X-Men
timeline.note: Bryan Singer's X-Men film casts James Marsden as Scott, the straight arrow sparring with Wolverine.

timeline.title: Phoenix-fueled and fallen
timeline.note: Possessed by the Phoenix in Avengers vs. X-Men, Scott strikes down his own mentor and becomes a mutant revolutionary.

timeline.title: Leading X-Men '97
timeline.note: The revival series X-Men '97 puts Scott back at the head of the team, and makes him a fan favorite all over again.
